For a supported atom and a null atom, every fiber at the supported start contains that start and has positive mass; compatible terms toward the null atom have zero numerator, and incompatible terms are zero. Thus the reverse transition toward the null atom vanishes without evaluating the supplied formula at a null start. Interchanging the atoms covers the other orientation.

The symmetric conditional-pair route is also valid: take X with law mu, choose the site independently and uniformly, and resample that site to obtain Y using the actual kernel. Conditional on the chosen site and a positive-mass retained fiber, X and Y are independent draws from the same conditional law of the full state on that fiber. Their product law is symmetric and assigns zero mass to pairs involving a null atom. A zero-mass fiber contributes zero to the joint law irrespective of the library's fixed version; off-fiber pairs also contribute zero. Averaging with the original site weights gives the symmetric joint flux mu(x) K(x,{y}) for all pairs.
